title: Resting-State EEG and Trait Anxiety
description: This dataset comprises resting-state EEG recordings from 51 right-handed undergraduate participants collected to investigate the relationship between resting-state EEG alpha/theta power, oscillatory dynamics, and trait anxiety. Participants completed a 4-minute alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed protocol while 256-channel EEG was recorded at 500 Hz. The dataset includes raw EEG data and phenotypic measures from standardized anxiety and personality questionnaires (STAI, TIPI, BIS/FFFS).
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a 256-channel EGI HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Net with Net Amps amplifier at 500 Hz sampling rate with online reference at Cz. The resting-state protocol consisted of alternating 1-minute eyes-open and eyes-closed blocks repeated twice. Preprocessing included bandpass filtering (0.1-50 Hz), line noise removal at 60 and 120 Hz, kurtosis-based channel rejection, average re-referencing, ICA decomposition, and artifact component removal via ICLabel with visual inspection.
